# Assignment

R accepts three assignment operators: `<-`, `=`, and `->`.

A variable name:

* can begin with a letter or a dot. E.g. `a <- 1`, `0 -> .a`
* cannot contain spaces — use `_` or `.` instead
* can contain numbers, just not as the first character. E.g. `a1 <- 1`

```{r error=TRUE}
v rsion <- 4.3.2 # invalid: a space inside the name breaks the parser
```

```{r}
a <- 1
b <- 2
0 -> .a
a1 <- .a
```

# Data Types

R has these core data types: numeric, integer, complex, character, logical,
raw, and factor.

## Numeric / double
Examples: `10.5`, `55`, `787`, `pi`.
```{r}
PI <- pi; class(PI); typeof(PI)
n <- 55; class(n); typeof(n)
```

## Integer
Append `L` to a literal to declare it as an integer (`1L`, `55L`, `100L`).
```{r}
n <- 55L
class(n)
```

## Complex
An example of a complex number is $9 + 3i$, where $i$ is the imaginary part.
Multiplying a real number by `1i` converts it to complex.
```{r}
z <- 9 + 3i
class(z)
typeof(z)

z1 <- a + 1i * b
print(z1)
class(z1)
```

## Character / string
```{r}
string <- "I am Learning R"
class(string)
```
Remember: `"LeaRning"` is different from `"Learning"` — R is case-sensitive.

## Logical / Boolean
```{r}
TRUE  # or T
FALSE # or F
```
A logical value is often the *result* of a test:
```{r}
"LeaRning" == "Learning"
```

## Raw
```{r}
text <- "I am learning R."
(raw_text <- charToRaw(text))
class(raw_text)
```
Converting raw back to text:
```{r}
rawToChar(raw_text)
```

## Factors
Factors represent qualitative/categorical data — colors, pass/fail, movie
ratings — and are the backbone of statistical modeling in R.
```{r}
Gender <- factor(c("Female", "Male"))
print(Gender)
class(Gender)
```

## Logical, revisited
```{r}
v <- TRUE
w <- FALSE

class(v); typeof(v)
!v

isTRUE(w)
```

## Creating objects directly

Numeric:
```{r}
n <- 10
x <- numeric(n) # a numeric vector of length n, filled with zeros
print(x)

x[1] <- 2.5
print(x)
```

Integer — note that assigning a decimal silently upgrades it to numeric:
```{r}
n <- 10
x <- integer(n)
print(x)
class(x)

x[1] <- 2.5 # R converts the whole vector to numeric
class(x)
print(x)
```

## Conversions

To convert between data types, use one of the `as.*()` functions from base
R. The naming convention is `as.` followed by the target type.

* Numeric to character
```{r}
n <- 55
n_char <- as.character(n)
print(n_char); class(n_char)
```

* Character to numeric
```{r}
s <- "123"
s_num <- as.numeric(s)
print(s_num); class(s_num)
```
A string that isn't a valid number becomes `NA` (with a warning) rather
than causing an error:
```{r}
suppressWarnings(as.numeric("abc"))
```

* Factor to character
```{r}
f <- factor(c("low", "high", "medium"))
f_char <- as.character(f)
print(f_char); class(f_char)
```

* Character to factor
```{r}
level <- "medium"
level_fct <- as.factor(level)
print(level_fct); class(level_fct)
```
